title: universalcefr-check: a provenance and redundancy check over the public UniversalCEFR collection
description:
Applies a declare-then-test provenance check to the 24 public corpora of the UniversalCEFR collection: 13 languages, 65,037 rows. The method is to find the source a dataset declares, then test the data against that declaration rather than trusting it.

Most of the collection is clean: one schema across all 24 corpora, the language field correct on every row, and no cross-corpus overlap anywhere in thirteen languages - with one exception. cambridge_exams_en is 99.7% contained in elg_cefr_en (324 of 325 texts, labels agreeing on 324 of 324) while the two declare different repositories, different papers and different licences, so agreement between them is not corroboration.

Three corpora repeat their own texts under conflicting CEFR levels: cople2_pt (471 texts each present twice, as A1/A2, B1/B2, C1/C2), elg_cefr_nl (1,195 texts stored as 3,596 rows), and caes_es (the placeholder string "none" 214 times across five levels). One listed dataset, ComplexityMT, has no data files. Collection-wide, 13,611 of 65,037 rows duplicate another row, so a random split leaks.

What the check cannot determine from outside is whether any of this originates upstream or in the conversion to the UniversalCEFR format; the two produce identical output. Fully reproducible in one command, roughly four minutes. Redistributes no data - the script downloads the published exports, and each corpus keeps its own licence.
